sentences.text: Rajeev vs State Of U.P. on 17 May, 2023

Bench: Ajay Rastogi, Abhay S. Oka
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
 Miscellaneous Application No.384 of 2023
 in
 Civil Appeal No. 3763 of 2022
 Rajeev & Ors.

Applicants/Appellants
 versus
 State of U.P. & Ors.

Respondents
 O R D E R
1.
By the judgment and order dated 9 th May 2022, this Court disposed of the Civil Appeals.

The present Application seeks a clarification on what is held in paragraph 13 of the said judgment, which reads thus:
13.

In the case of Sahara India Commercial Corporation Limited and Others v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Others, this Court found that invocation of urgency clause under Section 17 was invalid and illegal.

entities.text: Sahara India Commercial Corporation Limited and Others v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court moulded the relief and directed payment of compensation in terms of the 2013 Act by treating the relevant date as the date of its judgment.

Therefore, we find no error in the approach of the High Court when it directed payment of market value computed as per the 2013 Act to those land owners who have not accepted the compensation under Karar Niyamawali by taking the date of the judgment as a deemed date after following the 2013 Act.
The High Court has done the balancing act by saving the acquisition proceedings while granting the aforesaid monetary relief to the land owners.

2. The submission of the learned senior counsel appearing for the Reason:
applicants is that though this Court has observed in paragraph 13 that the market value will be computed on the basis of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, the 2013 Act), the operative part of the impugned judgment of the High Court suggests that the compensation will be payable in terms of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894 (for short, the 1894 Act).

entities.text: Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, it is necessary to clarify that the compensation will be payable in terms of the 2013 Act.
The learned senior counsel appearing for the respondents submitted that no such clarification is warranted.

1 3.
The High Court found that the acquisition was vitiated due to noncompliance of Section 5A of the 1894 Act.

Instead of setting aside the acquisition, the High Court did a balancing act by directing that the compensation should be payable at the rate prevailing on the date of the impugned judgment of the High Court.

4. This Court approved the approach of the High Court of not setting aside the acquisition on the basis of another decision of this Court in the case of Sahara India Commercial Corporation Limited & Ors. v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors. 1

entities.text: Sahara India Commercial Corporation Limited & Ors. v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, after holding that invocation of urgency clause under Section 17 of the 1894 Act was illegal, this Court did not disturb the acquisition.
But, this Court directed that the payment of compensation shall be in terms of the 2013 Act by treating the relevant date as the date of its judgment.
5. Therefore, we clarify that in the peculiar facts of the case, computation of the compensation shall be made in accordance with the 2013 Act as on the date of the impugned judgment.

We have already approved the view taken by the High Court that this relief can be extended only to those who have not accepted the compensation under Karar Niyamawali.
6.
The Application is, accordingly, allowed by making aforesaid 1 (2017) 11 SCC 339 clarification confined to the cases covered by paragraph 13 of our judgment.

.J. (Ajay Rastogi) .J. (Abhay S. Oka) New Delhi;
May 17, 2023.
